key_insight: Euclid-MCP wraps deterministic Prolog reasoning in a standardized MCP tool server, letting LLMs offload multi-step logic while preserving proof traces and repair loops.
engineering_relevance: It offers a reusable, engine-agnostic way to add exact rule-based inference to agents and RAG systems in compliance- and safety-sensitive workflows.
method: Defines Euclid-IR, a human-readable Horn-clause intermediate representation.
Compiles Euclid-IR to SWI-Prolog or other backends for deterministic inference.
Exposes a translate-run-inspect-repair tool loop with proof and derivation logs.
evidence_signal: The paper reports evaluation on an IT security/compliance use case, finding that LLMs work on small knowledge bases but hallucinate on larger ones, while Euclid-MCP returns exact answers with lower latency and more compact outputs.
watch_item: Adoption depends on correct rule encoding and backend compilation, so errors in Euclid-IR translation or Prolog knowledge maintenance could still undermine results.
paper_title: Euclid-MCP: A Model Context Protocol Server for Deterministic Logical Reasoning via Prolog
